title: Now I'm Convinc'd the Lord Is Kind
description: Now I'm Convinc'd the Lord Is Kind in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 10 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 73, part 1, headed “Afflicted saints happy, and prosperous sinners cursed”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now I'm con-vinc'd the Lord is kind To men of heart sin-cere, Yet once my fool-ish thoughts re-pin'd And bor-der'd on de-spair.

lines: Now I'm convinc'd the Lord is kind
Yet once my foolish thoughts repin'd
I griev'd to see the wicked thrive,
"In vain I lift my hands to pray,
"For I am chasten'd all the day,
Yet while my tongue indulg'd complaints,
"Sure I shall thus offend thy saints,
But still I found my doubts too hard,
Till I retir'd to search thy word,
There, as in some prophetic glass,
High mounted on a slippery place,
I heard the wretch profanely boast,
Till at thy frown he fell;
His honours in a dream were lost,
Lord, what an envious fool I was!
Thus to suspect thy promis'd grace,
Yet I was kept from full despair,
That blessed hand that broke the snare
Shall guide me to thy throne.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
